outcomeNote: Rav Ḥisda's scoping of the dispute stands unchallenged in this unit.

segments.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס, אֲבָל בְּטוּמְטוּם — דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל סְפֵיקָא הוּא, וְקָדוֹשׁ מִסְּפֵיקָא.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And the Rabbis say:» A hermaphrodite «does not» have «firstborn» status; rather, its status is that of a non-sacred animal that may be shorn and utilized for labor. «Rav Ḥisda says:» This «dispute» applies «to a hermaphrodite,» which the Rabbis maintain is a distinct entity, as it has both male and female sex organs, and therefore it does not have firstborn status. «But with regard to a tumtum,» whose genitalia is covered by skin, «everyone agrees» that «it is an uncertain» case, as it is definitely either a male or a female, but there is uncertainty as to which it is. «And» consequently, it is «consecrated due to uncertainty,» and it may not be slaughtered either in the Temple or in the rest of the country.
